source.title: Vitamin and mineral requirements in human nutrition, 2nd edition — Chapter 13, Table 40: Recommended nutrient intakes for iron based on varying dietary iron bio-availabilities

notes: Values are transcribed verbatim from FAO/WHO Table 40. Nothing is interpolated.

FAO/WHO publishes the iron RNI at four dietary iron bio-availability levels because absorption, not intake, is the binding constraint. All four are shipped here; the app must not silently pick one without saying so in the UI copy.

defaultBioavailability is 10% — the moderate level FAO/WHO applies to infants and young children on a mixed diet. Peru's INS recipe corpus is built around heme sources (sangrecita, bazo, higado), which would justify 12%; 10% is the more conservative choice and therefore the safer default for a coverage figure a caregiver acts on.
FAO/WHO brackets the 6-11 month values in the published table, noting that bio-availability of dietary iron varies greatly during this period. The bracket is preserved as isBracketedInSource.

No MINSA or INS document publishing a dietary iron requirement table by age in mg/day was located. MINSA's anemia norms (NTS N.o 213-MINSA/DGIESP-2024, RM 250-2017) prescribe supplementation doses, which are a different quantity and must not be used as a dietary requirement. This is why an FAO/WHO source is used here.
weeklyMg is dailyMg x 7, computed here so the app never re-derives it inconsistently.
This table keys on AGE ONLY, never on hemoglobin — see ADR-0007.
